result.title: Chalk on Church Lane
result.text: You broke No. 14, then the Pells’ house next door. I had marked my own door with the circle for empty; I kept the chalk. There were eleven boxes I could not carry, and an untuned piano in the room. Mrs Pell had a receipt for roof repairs and told everyone she had voted against the levy. She still came to every drill and knocked through her list. Later, Riverside dam gave way. Gil Harrow wrote that the spillway had been deferred twice: inspectors called the dam satisfactory; the harbour needed dredging; the school roof leaked; he thought there was time. St Bride’s remained intact. Its hall opened as a rest point, with the tea urn on from five. I have the notice, and the chalk.
